subject: Telemetry disclosure & derivative ownership — evidence pack request
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@oakridgehealth.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@oakridgehealth.com
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot DPA questions — telemetry & model-use

Hi Lauren / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of specifics we need for legal/infosec signoff before we proceed with the pilot:

- We need an explicit no-training (no model improvement) commitment covering prompts, responses, and other interaction telemetry for the pilot scope.
- What telemetry do you retain by default (request/response, timestamps, IPs, agent strings, latency metrics)? We need a short disclosure we can attach to our DPA.
- If some telemetry is required for operational monitoring, can you produce an "evidence pack" proving it is ephemeral / not used for model training? Examples: retention windows, who has access, deletion workflow, and subprocessor lists.

Can you also confirm whether any subprocessors in the ASIA region will see data for this pilot (we plan to keep data in US regions only)?

If you can send a short summary + attachments we can circulate with procurement/legal. We are aiming to finalize paperwork next week.

Appreciate it,
Sarah

--
Sarah Liu
Sr. Procurement Manager | Oakridge Health
sarah.liu@oakridgehealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@oakridgehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot DPA questions — telemetry & model-use

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front:

- No-training commitment: for the hosted pilot we can commit in writing that customer interactions will not be used to train or improve Redwood models. We can include explicit language in the DPA and a one-way operational attest.
- Telemetry retained: minimal operational telemetry by default — request ID, timestamps, latency metrics, and an ephemeral KV cache for session routing. We do NOT log full prompts to long-term telemetry unless the customer enables debug mode. IPs are collected at the edge for rate-limiting and regional routing but can be redacted in downstream logs.
- Evidence pack: we can produce an ops evidence bundle that includes retention windows, access lists (roles), a subprocessor snapshot, and a short runbook showing deletion.

I've attached an operational checklist that outlines what we can provide quickly. Key tradeoffs / asks from our side: we need the ability to collect short-term telemetry for latency/availability SLOs and to preserve an ephemeral cache for interactive sessions — we propose a 48-hour default retention that is purged by automated jobs unless you request a different window.

On subprocessors: we will ensure no ASIA-region processor has access for the Oakridge pilot — all processing will be routed to our US-hosted clusters and onshore KMS for key operations. I will confirm the subprocessor snapshot for the exact date the evidence is produced.

Next steps: if this direction looks acceptable, we can (1) circulate the DPA clause language for the no-training guarantee, (2) provide the ops evidence checklist (attached), and (3) schedule a short handshake call with your security team this week.

[Attachment: ops-evidence-checklist.pdf]

Best,
Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Head of Privacy & Partner Compliance | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com

From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@oakridgehealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot DPA questions — telemetry & model-use

Sarah — looping in a couple legal-level redlines and clarifications. Quick summary below; I attached a marked DPA with proposed language.

1) No-training / non‑derivative clause: we will accept a clause that prohibits us from using customer-provided prompts/responses to improve our global models. We request a carveout for safety debugging: in the event of an incident (P1/P0), we may access debug captures under strict access controls for remediation. We propose incident-capture as an explicit exception with audit trail.

2) Prompt/response ownership: Oakridge retains ownership of prompts and derivatives. To operationalize this we propose an explicit exportability promise and a deletion SLA (30 days for pilot artifacts on request; 48-hour auto purge otherwise).

3) Telemetry disclosure: we'll produce the evidence bundle (roles, retention, KMS zone, subprocessor list as of the evidence snapshot). Please note our subprocessor list may include managed logging providers in the US that hold ephemeral logs; we will not use those logs for training.

4) Subprocessors & cross-border: Kimble (our logging provider) is US-only for your pilot. If Oakridge requires a formal onshore-only attestation that includes code-level attestations, we can add that as a contract addendum and provide SOC 2 Type II report references.

5) Attachments / delivery: attached is a draft DPA redline focused on the above; also added two short clauses for escrow/derivative custody if you want an extrajudicial safeguard.

[Attachment: dpa-redlines-llm.docx]

If you can confirm you want the incident-capture carveout we proposed (and the 48‑hour default retention), we can finalize language and push the evidence bundle by Thursday.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@oakridgehealth.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, procurement@oakridgehealth.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 17:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot DPA questions — telemetry & model-use

Thanks Lauren/Kimberly — this is helpful and addresses most of our questions. A few clarifications from procurement/security before we sign:

- We accept the 48-hour default retention for telemetry and the 30-day deletion SLA on request.
- Incident-capture carveout is acceptable provided (a) access is logged in an immutable audit trail, (b) access is limited to a named incident response team, and (c) we receive a brief incident summary when data is accessed.
- Please confirm the SOC 2 report reference and provide the subprocessor snapshot URL.

Procurement wants the revised DPA with your redlines and an evidence bundle uploaded to the shared Drive by Thursday so we can run the legal review. If you can also drop a short DocuSign link to the revised DPA that would speed signing.

We will schedule a 30-minute security handshake for Wednesday 10–10:30 PT — can you confirm names to invite?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — confident we can close next week.

Best,
Sarah

--
Sarah Liu
Sr. Procurement Manager | Oakridge Health
